chunks: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Sa'd Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid. He said: Abu al-Qasim al-Kufi narrated to us from Hannan ibn Sadir from his father. He said: I said to Abu Ja'far al-Baqir (peace be upon him):

'Can a son repay his father?' He replied: 'There is no recompense for him except in two qualities: that the father be a slave, so he buys him and sets him free, or that there be a debt upon him, so he pays it off on his behalf.'

key_terms.الوالد: The father — the parent whose rights are supreme
key_terms.خصلتين: Two qualities/cases — the only means of true repayment
key_terms.يجزي: To repay or compensate — fulfilling a debt of gratitude

ai.seo_question: How can a son repay his father according to Imam al-Baqir?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) teaches that a son can only truly repay his father's rights in two specific cases: if the father is enslaved, the son purchases and frees him; or if the father has debts, the son pays them off. This hadith, from the assembly of Shaykh al-Saduq in 368 AH, reflects the immense value Islam places on parental rights — emphasizing that ordinary filial duties can never fully compensate a parent's sacrifices.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. Musa b. al-Mutawakkil (ra) narrated to us. He said: `Ali b. al-Husayn al-Sa`d Abadi narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid. He said: Abu’l Qasim al-Kufi narrated to us from Hannan b. Sadir from his father. He said: I said to Abi Ja`far al-Baqir (as):

’Can a son pay back (for the favors of) a father?’ The Imam replied, ‘There is no payment for him except two things: if the father is a slave and the son buys him and sets him free, or the father is in debt and the son pays it off.’
